Order Order

No. 12.09.2024  02.
 1.
The petitioner is an accused in connection with Bahalda P.S. Case No.48 of 2024 corresponding to C.T. Case No.464 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 451/376(2)/379/420/506/34 of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M., Rairangpur, District-Mayurbhanj.
The petitioner had approached the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rairangpur in BLAPL No.19 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 02.05.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.

The prosecution case as per the F.I.R. is that, on 04.04.2024 at about 10 A.M., the complainant reported at Bahalda P.S. alleging that the present petitioner had been exploiting her and has taken a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- from her.
On 16.11.2023, he entered into her house at Banadunguri and abducted her from her house in a car and demanded Rs.4,80,000/- and forcefully kept sexual relationship with her.
He threatened to kill her daughter and husband, if she contacted her husband.

Hence, the F.I.R.

1 4.
The charge sheet has been filed on 31.05.2024.

The statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 of the Cr. P.C., from which it reveals that the husband of the victim started doubting her regarding her relationship with the present petitioner.
Therefore, on 16.11.2023, she fled away with the present petitioner and stayed with him in a rented house.

Subsequent thereto on 04.04.2024,
the initial F.I.R. was filed by the husband of the victim.
Reading of the statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. also reveals that the relationship seems be a consensual one.
The petitioner has been in custody since 04.04.2024.

5. Regard being had to the period of custody of the petitioner since 04.04.2024 and the nature of acquisition, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.
6.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:
(1) The petitioner shall appear before the Court, without fail, on every date of hearing; and (2) He shall not influence any of the witnesses related to this case in any manner whatsoever.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
7. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
